transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... my wife told me I needed to make an appointment. I guess... I've just been starting a lot of projects lately, and I can't really seem to stop. 

Just things like... drafting new work plans, setting up certification schedules, upgrading the home network... sending out messages to old contacts. I don't know, it just gets intense and I kind of blow past normal limits, I guess. It got to the point where my wife and my director at work had to step in and say something. So... that's why I'm here.
How long has this been going on—days, weeks, or longer?
Um... longer. It's been... I guess about two years and five months. It started when I took on a major system migration role at work. So... yeah. Since then.

Since this began two and a half years ago, has this high level of energy and drive been pretty much constant, or does it come in waves—like periods where you feel this way, followed by other periods where your mood or energy drops back down or even gets low?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't exactly tracked it. 

I guess... it's just been a really busy couple of years. I haven't really noticed if it drops down or not. I'm not sure.
Over these past two and a half years, have you been using any substances regularly—like alcohol, stimulants, caffeine pills, or other drugs?
Um... no. I don't really do any of that. Just... no.
During this time, have you noticed a change in how much sleep you need—like feeling fully rested and energetic after only a few hours of sleep?

Um... yeah, sometimes. There have been... stretches where I only get about three hours. I'll wake up at maybe 3 or 4 a.m. and... I don't know, I just feel sharp. Like I've been given extra time to get things done, not really tired at all.

During these high-energy stretches, has it ever gotten severe enough to cause serious problems—like losing your job, being hospitalized, or having thoughts or beliefs that others felt were unrealistic or out of touch with reality?

Um... no, no hospitals or anything. But... I guess there have been some issues. 

At work, they... they put me on leave for a bit. After a migration failed. And at home... my wife has had to step in a lot more lately. Just with things like watching the spending, or... getting on me about working late into the night. It usually just turns into arguments. 

I don't know. I've also kind of pulled away from other things... like church music, climbing... mentoring. I just couldn't reliably show up or follow through anymore, so... yeah.
Thinking about the times when you've felt this energized and needed less sleep, how long does that particular stretch usually last before things settle back down—days, a week, or longer?

Um... I don't really track the exact days. I just know that... these stretches where I'm unusually driven and, I guess, overconfident... they've been a part of my life for roughly a year and eight months now. I haven't really timed them beyond that.

When you're in one of these energized, driven stretches, does it typically last continuously for at least a full week before you feel more like your usual self, or does it usually settle back down after just a few days?
I... I don't really know. Like I said, I don't track it like that. It's just... a stretch of time. I haven't counted the days.
Focusing on the specific stretch of time when you were put on leave at work, do you recall roughly how many days in a row that episode of high energy and overconfidence lasted before it eased up?
I'm... not sure. It's hard to remember exactly. It was a while ago and... things were just really busy. I didn't count the days.

During that period when you were put on leave, was your functioning affected so severely that you were essentially unable to work or carry out your usual responsibilities at all, or were you still managing to function, just less effectively than usual?

I mean... I wasn't working. Like I said, they put me on leave after the... the server migration thing didn't work out. And at home... my wife kind of took over. She had to step in because of... well, the spending, and I was working late into the night. We were arguing a lot. I... I also stopped doing my usual stuff. I wasn't going to church to play music, wasn't climbing, wasn't doing my mentoring thing. I just... couldn't really show up for any of it.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a distinct period of elevated, expansive mood with increased goal-directed activity (multiple simultaneous projects), decreased need for sleep (functioning on 3 hours without fatigue), inflated self-confidence/overconfidence, excessive involvement in activities with painful consequences (impulsive spending requiring wife's intervention), and marked impairment in occupational (placed on leave after work failure) and social functioning (withdrawal from church music, climbing, mentoring; marital conflict). No psychotic symptoms (hallucinations/delusions) or hospitalization occurred, ruling out severe-with-psychotic-features. No substance use to account for symptoms. The episode's severity causing occupational and social impairment, combined with the symptom cluster, meets criteria for a manic episode without psychotic features. Longitudinal course (~2.5 years with more recent 20-month stretch of pronounced symptoms) suggests this is part of Bipolar I Disorder, currently manic.
